limitations: Smithery reports connection state only; it exposes no upstream account identity, so claims carry that limitation and no exact-account verification is asserted.
Upstream revocation is unsupported: deleting a managed connection ends the brokered session and does not revoke the provider grant.
Runtime calls need a host-supplied McpClientPort; without one the invoke capability row is unsupported.
Live evidence blocked: no authorized Smithery namespace or service token in this environment.
workItems.notes: createSmitheryConnectionsAdapter, id "smithery", custody external-execution-broker. Namespace and connection id come from the reviewed binding settings and are checked against permittedTargets; a token that cannot reach the selected connection fails closed (no broad-token fallback, no namespace creation, no substituted connection). Runtime tokens are minted per call through POST /tokens scoped to {namespaces, resources: connections, operations: [read, execute], metadata, ttl 1h}; the deployment API key is never the bearer of a runtime call. The MCP destination is the binding's approved origin plus the approved namespace, and tools are addressed as {connectionId}.{toolName}.

limitations: Local execution is unavailable by default: unavailableHostRunner reports the exact reason and the invoke capability row is unsupported with runtime trusted-local-runner.
Docker publishes no JSON schema for the catalog file; the field set was taken from the documentation and from the served catalog, and unknown fields are noted by name rather than carried.
Entries whose authorization is performed by the Docker MCP Toolkit are preserved with a blocking authorize diagnostic; Ceremony does not run the Toolkit.
Export is only possible for definitions that originated from a Docker catalog; values redacted on import are never reconstructed.
workItems.notes: readDockerMcpCatalog(text) parses with yaml 2.9.0 under uniqueKeys, core schema, YAML 1.2, silent log level and a bounded alias count, then measures depth/nodes/bytes and refuses reserved object keys before interpreting any field. createDockerMcpCatalogAdapter, id "docker-mcp-catalog", support catalog-only. exportDockerMcpDescriptor(definition) round-trips an entry with a loss report; dockerRunDescriptor(definition) builds the descriptor a HostRunnerPort would need without running anything.

limitations: PulseMCP documents /v0beta as deprecated with a sunset by September 2026; the capability row carries that sentence.
The native listing exposes no version, tools or configuration schema, so definitions record that rather than inventing them.

Sub-registry entries wrap a server.json document; importing one requires the MCP registry importer to be wired in, otherwise the import capability row is unsupported and the entry stays discoverable only.
Live evidence blocked: no PulseMCP tenant API key in this environment.
workItems.notes: createPulseMcpAdapter, id "pulsemcp", support catalog-only. The native profile pages with offset/count_per_page and never follows PulseMCP's absolute next link; the sub-registry profile pages with cursor/limit behind X-API-Key and X-Tenant-ID read through ConfigurationPort. Discovery results are cached per tenant, binding revision and configuration revision with a bounded TTL (default 5 minutes, capped at one hour); on an outage the previous snapshot is returned with freshness.stale true and a pulsemcp.refresh.failed diagnostic, and a cold outage fails rather than reporting an empty catalog.

limitations: Suggestions only: the module merges nothing and exposes no way to accept a suggestion; acceptance is a separate host action.
Evidence is limited to repository identity, remote origin and qualified name. A shared display name never produces a suggestion.
Same-ecosystem duplicates are excluded unless includeSameEcosystem is set, because a source's own duplicates are that source's problem.
workItems.notes: suggestEquivalences(items, options) returns EquivalenceSuggestion { members, confidence, reasons, limitations }. Confidence is the number of independent shared identities (high: two or more kinds; medium: repository or qualified name; low: remote origin alone), never a probability.

contractChanges.description: destinationUrl rejects any %2F in a path, which is right for a path template but wrong for a single path segment that legitimately contains a slash (Smithery documents encoding a qualified name as namespace%2Fserver). A local helper smitheryUrl(destination, basePath, segments) in src/server/connectors/registries/smithery/api.ts repeats every other destinationUrl check (absolute base path, no encoded slash in the template, one segment per entry, exact origin, path prefix, no `..` after decoding) and appends already-encoded segments. Proposal: add destinationUrlFromSegments(destination, template, segments) to binding.ts with the same rules and have the Smithery modules use it.
contractChanges.compatibility: Additive; no existing shape changes. The local helper stays valid if the proposal is declined.

integrationPatches.description: Register createSmitheryRegistryAdapter() from registries/smithery/index.ts (id smithery-registry, catalog-only), createSmitheryConnectionsAdapter({ mcpClient }) from providers/smithery/index.ts (id smithery, external-execution-broker), createDockerMcpCatalogAdapter() from registries/docker/index.ts (id docker-mcp-catalog, catalog-only) and createPulseMcpAdapter({ importServerJson }) from registries/pulsemcp/index.ts (id pulsemcp, catalog-only).

McpClientFactory in providers/smithery/ports.ts is a structural narrowing of the MCP swarm's McpClient: wire it as ({ endpoint, bearer, fetch }) => createMcpClient({ profile, endpoint, fetch, auth: { kind: "bearer", use: bearer.use } }). Their callTool outcome union is assignable to McpToolOutcome. Without this the Smithery invoke capability row reports unsupported, which is accurate rather than broken.

createPulseMcpAdapter accepts importServerJson(document, { location?, capturedAt }) => NormalizedDefinition[]. Wire it to importServerJson from registries/mcp/import.ts so PulseMCP sub-registry entries are imported by the official server.json importer instead of a second implementation of that schema. The PulseMCP module reads only the envelope and the com.pulsemcp/* _meta extensions.

suggestEquivalences is cross-source by nature and does not belong inside any one registry directory, so it was created as a new file at registries/cross-source.ts rather than edited into a shared file. Move it if the integrator prefers another home; it imports only ../adapter.js types.

None of these modules are exported from src/core/index.ts or src/server/index.ts by this swarm. They are server-only and must not enter the browser bundle; export them from the server barrel only if the reference app needs them.

The HostRunnerPort therefore takes a descriptor and leaves command construction to the host runner instead of guessing a gateway invocation.
Docker publishes no machine-readable schema for the catalog file; unknown per-entry fields are reported by name and not carried.

Smithery's error bodies for a service token that lacks a connection are documented only as 401/403/404 with {error, message}; the double follows the documented shape and the adapter maps status codes, but the exact upstream body was not observed.
PulseMCP /v0beta premium enrichment fields (authOptions, tools) exist only on the /v0.1 sub-registry; they are read as provenance there and are not normalized into capabilities.
